summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of mechanical aortic valve replacement, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, coronary artery disease, peripheral vascular disease, and prior right below-knee amputation was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and hypertensive urgency. She presented with uncontrolled hypertension, elevated troponin likely due to demand ischemia, and an anion gap metabolic acidosis attributed to sodium thiosulfate from dialysis. A CT head revealed a nonspecific medullary hyperdensity, but the patient declined recommended MRI follow-up. She was transferred to Vascular Surgery and underwent a left first and second toe amputation due to dry gangrene, with the procedure scaled down as the gangrene had improved. Her blood pressure was stabilized with a regimen of labetalol, amlodipine, and hydralazine, and anticoagulation was bridged with heparin before restarting warfarin. She recovered well postoperatively, with controlled symptoms and a clean wound, and was discharged home with visiting nurse services for wound care and follow-up appointments in vascular surgery and nephrology.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Heart valve replaced by other means
